questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of open/closed principles, plugin registries, and runtime configurability for cross-cutting concerns like logging.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern
- Registry / plugin architecture
- Thread-safety and dynamic configuration
- Separation of concerns in logging

## Code Example
```javascript
interface LogEvent { level: string; message: string; ts: number; }
interface LogFormatter { format(event: LogEvent): string; }
class JSONFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return JSON.stringify(e); } }
class KVFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return `ts=${e.ts} level=${e.level} msg='${e.message}'`; } }
class Registry<T> { private map = new Map<string, T>(); register(name: string, v: T){ this.map.set(name, v); } get(name: string): T | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle thread-safety in a multi-threaded environment?
- How to test registering and switching formatters in isolation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Introduce a new angle: runtime-extensible evaluation logic for feature flags to reflect real-world needs in large orgs.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for evaluators
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Composite rule composition (anyOf/allOf)
- EvalContext design and caching for performance

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: EvalContext): boolean }
type EvalContext = { user: any; time: Date; attrs: any }
class EvaluatorRegistry {
  register(name: string, factory: (cfg: any)=>Evaluator): void
  resolve(name: string, cfg: any): Evaluator
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to model evaluation order and short-circuit semantics?
- How to handle cross-feature conflicts and auditing of evaluator registrations?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design for runtime extensibility and reliability in a pluggable notification system.

## Key Concepts

- **Registry-driven plugins**: Channels are registered at runtime via a central registry, enabling new channel types without recompiling the core dispatcher.
- **Channel interface and factories**: A standardized contract ensures all notification channels implement common behavior while factories handle instantiation.
- **Per-user preferences**: Respect individual user settings for preferred notification channels and delivery priority.
- **Fallback strategy**: A reliable rollback mechanism ensures notifications are delivered even when primary channels fail.

- Strategy/Plugin patterns for checks and aggregators
- Runtime registries with factories
- Hot-reload and zero-downtime swaps
- Per-service overrides and versioned strategies

## Code Example
```javascript
class HealthCheck { async check() { /* return {ok:true} */ } }
class Aggregator { aggregate(results) { /* return aggregated status */ } }
class Registry { register(name, factory) { /* ... */ } create(name) { return factory(); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle circular dependencies between checks?
- How would you test a new check without affecting live services?
